Hi Priyom / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement has reviewed the draft order form and our finance team flagged the pricing exhibit — specifically the hard floor and the lack of a mechanism for short-term burst overages. Two asks from our side:

1) Introduce a "smoothing band" instead of a strict floor so that transient spikes (up to ~30% for short windows) do not immediately trigger true-ups. We would expect a quarterly true-up but prefer an averaging method over the quarter.

2) Add a reflected "burst credit" (one-time credit bucket) for the first two quarters to cover onboarding spikes while we optimize usage patterns. This should not change the permanent minimum commitment.

We attached an annotated spreadsheet with our expected usage curve and an annotated PDF with the redlines we propose (high level). We are open to a compromise (temporary credit + a smaller smoothing band) but need something in the contract for our CFO to sign off.

Attachments: Cloudline_RFP_Prices.xlsx; Annotated_OrderForm_Cloudline.pdf

Can we get Redwood's proposed language and a short summary of operational impacts (how burst credits are consumed, how smoothing is measured) by EOD Wednesday PT? Also: available for a 30-min sync tomorrow 11:00 PT?

Ethan — thanks for the clear ask and the annotated files. We can take the following approach as a compromise that preserves revenue protection while addressing Cloudline's operational concerns:

- Smoothing band: define a 20% smoothing band on short-term variance (per invoice period) with a quarterly rolling-average true-up. This prevents one-off spikes from immediately causing floor true-ups but keeps quarterly settlement intact.

- Burst credit: offer a one-time onboarding credit pool equal to 10% of the first quarter estimated spend (applied as token credits consumed before billing) valid for the first two billing cycles. This would be explicit in the order form as a temporary credit and would not alter the committed minimums.

Operational notes (high level):
- Smoothing measured on 24-hour rolling windows, aggregated into invoice periods; true-up uses quarter-average consumption above committed baseline.
- Burst credits are consumed FIFO against overage tokens and reported in the console line item "Onboarding Credits".

Attachments: Draft_OrderForm_Reply_Redlines.pdf (contains the proposed contract language and a redline of the pricing exhibit).

Forwarding my quick take after looking at Ethan's proposals overnight. Priyom — good compromise outline. A few guardrails from GTM that I'd like to preserve:

- We can authorize the onboarding credit up to 10% of Q1 estimated spend, but it must be explicitly time-boxed (expires after two billing cycles) and non-recoupable after consumption. No permanent floor adjustments.
- Legal should avoid introducing language that allows the customer to "count" credits toward the committed minimum. Credits are for overage protection only.
- If we do a smoothing band, it should be narrowly scoped to prevent gaming: 20% smoothing for spikes shorter than 7 days, with quarterly true-up that can be netted against future invoices (not used to reduce committed baseline).

Please loop in pricing ops (Ben) to confirm reporting & billing mechanics. Karhtik (sic) — can you draft firm language for the Order Form exhibit that captures the above while also including a revenue protection clause that preserves Redwood's minimums?

Team / Ethan — legal has reviewed and I'm attaching proposed amendment language (OrderForm_Amendment_v3.docx). High level summary of the edits and rationale: 

- Smoothing band: we define "Smoothing Band" as a symmetric 20% variance band measured on invoice-period consumption, with a quarterly rolling-average true-up. We explicitly limit the smoothing band to exclude sustained growth above the committed baseline (any sustained increase beyond two consecutive quarters triggers re-negotiation of baseline rates).

- Burst credit: redlined as a one-time credit pool equal to 10% of Customer's first-quarter estimated spend; credits are applied to overage charges only, cannot be used to reduce or offset the committed minimum, and expire after two billing cycles. We added anti-abuse language to prevent credits being stacked or carried forward.

- Revenue protection: included a clause that protects Redwood's economic position by allowing a netting true-up against future invoices and a right to re-evaluate committed minimums if usage patterns materially change for two consecutive quarters.

- Reporting & audit: added a requirement for Cloudline to provide usage reports on a weekly basis during the first 90 days; Redwood will surface consumption and credit usage in the console and will provide a monthly consumption export for reconciliation.

Ethan — if that aligns with Cloudline's expectations we can prepare a clean amendment and circulate for signature. Priyom / Marissa / Ben — please confirm the numeric parameters (20% smoothing, 10% credit) or propose adjustments.
